title: How can long rows of strokes be counted quickly?
description: A teacher drew one stroke for each child who chose a sweet, and the row grew long. The video bundles the strokes in fives and reads them back, and Keeko doubts whether the line across a bundle is a sixth mark.
teaching_notes: One idea: a tally mark is one stroke for each thing counted, and the fifth stroke is drawn across the first four. Watch for children who count the crossing line as an extra mark.

source: Tally marks: counting in bundles of five
video_script.why: The child sees why a line across four strokes makes a bundle of five that is quick to read.
video_script.substitution: the eight children who chose hockey in the favourite-games list
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}} at the board, drawing a stroke for each child's choice
video_script.wrong_answer: a bundle with its line is six
video_script.wrong_move: counts the crossing line as one more mark
video_script.payoff_line: The tally for hockey is one bundle of five and three strokes, which makes eight children.

names.{{NAME_2}}: teacher who buys sweets by the class preferences

maths_rules: Four strokes and the line across them make one bundle of 5.
5 + 3 = 8, so one bundle and three strokes show 8 children.
The hockey count of 8 comes from the book's favourite-games list.
video_script.design: Strokes appear one by one; at the fifth, a line sweeps across the first four and they turn into one bundle.

beats.on_screen: title card with a teacher at the board, a long row of single strokes beside five sweets

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the teacher and the sweets
marks.stroke: one stroke appears on the board for each child's choice
marks.ask: the row of strokes grows long and a question mark lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an idea from your book, where {{NAME_2}} asked children to choose a sweet.
<bookmark mark='stroke'/>For each child, the teacher drew one stroke on the board.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Soon the strokes made a long row that was hard to count.
How can such strokes be counted quickly?

beats.on_screen: the long row of strokes and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a card shows one stroke labelled tally mark, then four strokes with a line drawn across them to form a bundle

marks.stroke: one stroke is labelled with the words tally mark
marks.bundle: a line is drawn across four strokes to make a bundle of five

narration: <bookmark mark='stroke'/>One stroke drawn for each thing counted is called a tally mark.
<bookmark mark='bundle'/>When the count reaches five, a line is drawn across the four strokes.
That makes a bundle of five, which the eye reads at once.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eight children chose hockey.

beats.on_screen: To find: the tally marks for hockey, read back

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw the tally marks for hockey and read them back.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: four strokes, one for each of the first four children

marks.four: four strokes appear one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step one, draw four strokes, one for each of the first four children.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the fifth child makes a line across the four strokes, giving one bundle

marks.line: a line sweeps across the four strokes and they join into one bundle

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Step two, the fifth child makes the line across the four strokes.
This gives one bundle of five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: three more strokes beside the bundle, one for each of the last three children

marks.three: three strokes appear beside the bundle

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, draw one stroke for each of the three children left.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: read the tally: the bundle is 5, then add the 3 strokes: 5 + 3

marks.read: the bundle is counted as five and the three strokes are added to it

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step four, read the tally by counting the bundle as five and adding the three strokes.

beats.on_screen: Answer: one bundle of 5 and 3 strokes make 8 children
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The tally for hockey is one bundle of five and three strokes, which makes eight children.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bundle with a cross over the word six, and the four strokes plus the line counted one by one as five

marks.doubt: the word six appears beside the bundle and is crossed out
marks.fix: the four strokes and the line are counted one by one up to five

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a bundle with its line is six, because the line is one more mark.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the line is itself the fifth mark, and it crosses the other four.
Four strokes and the line make five, never six.
